steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Normative social influence (NSI): conforming to be accepted and avoid rejection - leads to compliance. Driven by the desire for social approval.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Informational social influence (ISI): conforming because we believe the group is correct - leads to internalisation. Most likely in ambiguous or novel situations.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Agentic State theory (Milgram): people obey because they enter an 'agentic state' - they see themselves as instruments carrying out another's wishes, not responsible for their actions. Binding factors (politeness, fear of disruption) keep people in the agentic state.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Legitimacy of authority: we obey people we perceive as having legitimate power (uniform, institutional context). When authority is perceived as illegitimate, obedience decreases (Milgram's run-down office: 48% vs 65% at Yale).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between normative and informational social influence. | Describe Milgram's agentic state theory and evaluate its usefulness for understanding obedience. | Explain how minority influence can lead to social change.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: NSI: driven by desire to be liked/accepted, leads to compliance, occurs when the correct answer is obvious. ISI: driven by desire to be correct, leads to internalisation, occurs in ambiguous situation | The agentic state explains how ordinary people commit harmful acts - they feel they are 'just following orders'. Supported by Milgram's variations. Limitations: doesn't explain why some people resist; | Social change through minority influence: (1) Minority is consistent - creates cognitive conflict. (2) Minority shows commitment - augmentation principle. (3) Minority is flexible - avoids seeming dog

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: NSI = want to be LIKED. ISI = want to be RIGHT. Agentic state = 'I'm just following orders.' Autonomous state = 'I'm making my own choices.' Minority influence needs: Consistency + Commitment + Flexibility = CCF.
